sources.title: Working with Quantized Types — NVIDIA TensorRT
sources.snippet: FP8E4M3 (FP8, 8-bit floating point with 4 exponent and 3 mantissa bits) FP4E2M1 (FP4, 4-bit floating point with 2 exponent and 1 mantissa bit) These low-precision formats allow TensorRT to deliver efficient inference while maintaining accuracy, making it suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments and high-throughput applications.

sources.snippet: Key Observations FP8-Static tends to have the best single-request latency (c=1 baseline), likely due to pre-computed scales avoiding runtime overhead. FP8-Dynamic and FP8-Static perform similarly at high concurrency, both significantly better than FP8-Block at c=100 for 31B. FP8-Block shows throughput regression at c=100 for 31B — the block-wise kernel may not be as optimized for high-batch ...
